clusters.name: codex-core-seam
clusters.executionModeRationale: A single codex-submodule story (feature-gated on_task_finished re-check placed after active_turn is cleared, + placement-guarded regression test + marker + patch-surface row); runs as its own codex impl job. The model policy moved to happy-cli, so there is no same-repo sibling to conflict with.

clusters.name: happy-cli-enablement-and-policy
clusters.executionModeRationale: All happy-cli, disjoint repo from the codex cluster, so codeable in parallel with Phase 1 codex work. US-002 (developerInstructions policy), US-003 (dual -c flags in both spawn paths + unsolicited-active-turn tracking), and US-004 (doctor readiness contract) share runCodex.ts and the new setting module, so keep them in ONE happy-cli impl job (serial within the job). Live validation (US-005) depends on the codex cluster being built.

clusters.name: live-validation-gate
clusters.executionModeRationale: End-to-end live validation against a codex build with the seam + a happy-cli build with the toggle; emits a structured decision artifact (unsolicitedTurnRendered, stalePromiseObserved, operatorDuringUnsolicitedTurn, transcriptRetrievalUsable, decision) that gates the conditional LOW-B cluster.

clusters.name: happy-cli-low-b-fallback
clusters.executionModeRationale: CONDITIONAL — implemented only if the validation gate decides low-b-required. Step 1 preserves process_id/source through the exec_command_end mapping (the discriminator), then a separate-route consumer pushes into MessageQueue2. Serialized after the gate; single-producer invariant means codex auto-wake is disabled for this path so there is no double prompt.
